perSite.title: Per-site cost difference (R_P vs S_AR)
perSite.gainNote: Gain = dummy cost − controller cost (saving, paper convention). Dashed = perfect-prediction upper bound (physical LP oracle, per-site); dotted = dummy zero; controllers are discrete points (no lines). Rank by 24h RMSE or site id.
perSite.note: Δ = R_P cost − S_AR cost per site; blue = R_P cheaper, grey = S_AR cheaper. Raw costs differ by ~0.3% on average, so the difference (not the scatter) carries the signal.

forecast.confidenceFamilyNote: R² = relative error reduction vs the constant-mean baseline — data predictability / explanatory power, not confidence; 70 sites, training periods, dataset forecast
forecast.siteRmseNote: RMSE = root mean square of forecast error (predicted net demand minus actual), in kWh per 15-min step; larger means larger average 24h-ahead forecast deviation (harder to predict). 70 sites ranked ascending by 24h-ahead net-demand forecast RMSE (log y-axis); 15min-ahead shown as reference. Absolute scale (no paper min-max normalization): same ordering direction as paper Fig. 3 but not numerically comparable
forecast.ctrlCompare: Controller one-step forecast comparison (test set, out-of-sample)
forecast.ctrlCompareNote: X axis = dataset forecast (k=1) 1-step RMSE on the test set (log scale); Y axis = controller forecast RMSE (log scale) — two scatter series: AR(1) (what S_AR actually uses) and persistence. The dashed y=x line is the equal-error line: points above it mean the dataset forecast is better, below it the controller forecast is better (further down-right = worse). AR(1) wins on 54/70 sites; on worst-scheduling sites 9/3 the SE forecast is better — forecast quality and scheduling performance are not simply causal. #62 is the only large net-export PV site, an RMSE scale outlier
forecast.curvesNote: All 70 sites available; default compares best-scheduling (33/59) vs worst-scheduling (9/3). Correlation, not causation. Window caveat: each site's curves come from the 2nd–3rd day (rows 97–288, 192 steps = 48h) of its own first test period; period start dates differ across sites, so cross-site comparison is structural (same relative window), not the same calendar dates
